rule: A code comment states its constraint in words and names no planning ordinal. Planning ordinals identify artifacts of a workflow that a future reader cannot resolve and that are renumbered as the plan is revised, so a citation accurate when written stops being so without anything changing. Durable external references are unaffected: they name something outside this repository's planning cycle and a reader can follow them.

placement.rule: A comment is the file header, or a `/** */` description attached to a module-level declaration, a member, a module-level literal element, or a test call. A comment anywhere else describes code that cannot carry it: move the reason into a description, or delete the comment.

checks.message: Section banner. Delete it. To group code, split the file, or give each declaration its own `/** */` description.
Comment on the same line as code. Move it into the `/** */` description of the declaration, or delete it.
Comment inside a function body. Move the reason into the function's `/** */` description, or delete the comment if the code already says it.
Description in `//` or `/* */` form. Write it as a `/** */` block.
Comment not attached to a declaration: a blank line follows it. Attach it as the `/** */` description of the next declaration, or delete it.
Comment on a statement that takes no description, such as an import, an expression, a parameter or a closing brace. Move it into a declaration's `/** */` description, or delete it.

prose.rule: A file header or a description is written in Simplified Technical English, in the pragmatic mode of the vendored `simple-english` skill, and it stays short. A reader who is not a native speaker reads a short sentence in a simple tense correctly, and the line budgets keep a comment in proportion to the code that it describes. The checks apply to comment text that is new or edited: a baselined block stays suppressed until someone changes it.

budgets.remedy: Cut the file header to the purpose of the file and the constraints that a reader must know. Move the detail onto the declarations that it describes.
budgets.reason: A header longer than one screen is not read. The budget counts lines of text: comment delimiters, blank lines and type-only JSDoc tags do not count. On the measured tree the median header had 13 lines of text, and the 90th percentile 34.

budgets.remedy: Cut the description to what the declaration does and why. Delete what the signature or the code already says.
budgets.reason: A description over 10 lines of text usually describes the body line by line. The budget counts lines of text, as the header budget does. On the measured tree the median description had 1 line of text, and the 90th percentile 8.

notForbidden.reason: Product vocabulary, not a planning ordinal. The workflow state machine has numbered phases and the append path has numbered phases; treating these as citations produced 45 false positives on the measured tree.

changelogPatterns.remedy: Describe what the code does now. A bare `previously` with no change narration is fine; this matches only the narrating form.
Describe present behavior. Version control holds the history.
Describe present behavior. Version control holds the history.
Describe present behavior. What a thing was called before is a question for `git log`.
changelogPatterns.disabledReason: Measured 42/50 (84%) on the tree, below the 95% floor. The 8 false positives are one coherent class: the verb describing a CONDITION rather than this code's history — a hypothetical ("if `@proof` were renamed"), a diagnostic ("the seam was moved or renamed, so the specifier resolved nothing"), a negation ("nothing was renamed — only the place the name is DECLARED moved"), a quoted example of the very phrasing being discussed, and a structural relative clause ("the routing construct a route was extracted from"). Narrowing to exclude conditional and diagnostic context is the path to enabling it; shipping at 84% would spend more review attention than it saves.

Measured 316 matches on the tree; adjudicating 22 put precision near 50%, far below the floor. Roughly half describe present or conditional behavior rather than narrating a change — "allowlist entries knip no longer flags", "unprobed rungs may no longer accumulate", "a build that no longer emits the shipped path would still...". Stays disabled.

precisionFloor.reason: A pattern that blocks below this rate spends more reviewer attention on false positives than it saves. Where fewer than sampleSize matches exist, all are adjudicated.

exemptPaths.reason: The policy states the patterns it forbids. A policy that cannot spell its own rule cannot declare it.
The classifier, extractor and baseline modules carry the rule's own vocabulary in remedies and docs.
The gate's own source names the patterns it reports.
The library tests assert on the patterns, so they must contain them.
The rule tests assert on the patterns, so they must contain them.
The gate's self-test writes offender text into its fixtures.
Kill fixtures carry verbatim offender text. A guard that flags its own fixtures cannot be tested.
Verbatim captured agent output. It is evidence of what an agent produced, not authored code: rewriting it would destroy the record.
